title: The completion of a Noetherian local ring has the same dimension
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] (a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mA^\wedge$). Then the Krull dimensions agree: $\dim A^\wedge=\dim A$ (both finite).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NV (lemma-completion-dimension), and its proof: A/m^n = A^/m^n A^ (Algebra Lemma 05GG), equal Hilbert functions, Algebra Proposition 00KQ (dimension = degree of the Hilbert polynomial); or the alternative given there: Algebra Lemma 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total) for the flat local map A -> A^ (Algebra Lemma 00MC) whose closed fibre A^/mA^ = A/m is a field

proof.text: (Setup.) Let $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ be the canonical map. $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]; it is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{A^\wedge}=\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ (the ideal generated by $\iota(\mathfrak m)$), and $\iota$ induces an isomorphism of fields $A/\mathfrak m\xrightarrow{\sim}A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]; and $\iota$ is flat (indeed faithfully flat) [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NV (lemma-completion-dimension), proof, the alternative proof: Algebra Lemma Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total); the hypotheses of 00ON for A -> A^ are Algebra Lemmas 0316, 05GG/05GI and 00MC

proof.text: (The maximal ideal of $A^\wedge$ lies over $\mathfrak m$.) $\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak mA^\wedge)$ contains $\mathfrak m$, since $\iota(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, and does not contain $1$, since $\iota(1)=1\notin\mathfrak mA^\wedge$, the maximal ideal of $A^\wedge$ (step 1). As $\mathfrak m$ is maximal, $\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak mA^\wedge)=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NV (lemma-completion-dimension), proof, the alternative proof: Algebra Lemma Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total)

proof.text: (The dimension formula.) Apply the flat dimension formula [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] to the flat map $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$ of Noetherian rings (step 1), the prime $\mathfrak Q=\mathfrak mA^\wedge$ and $\mathfrak p=\iota^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak m$ (step 2): $\dim(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak Q}=\dim A_{\mathfrak m}+\dim\big((A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak Q}/\mathfrak m(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak Q}\big)$. Since $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and $A^\wedge$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak Q$, the elements inverted in $A_{\mathfrak m}$, resp. $(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak Q}$, are already units, so the localization maps $A\to A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $A^\wedge\to(A^\wedge)_{\mathfrak Q}$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Hence $\dim A^\wedge=\dim A+\dim(A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total), applied as in More on Algebra Lemma 07NV, alternative proof

proof.text: (The closed fibre is a field; finiteness.) By step 1, $A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge\cong A/\mathfrak m$ is a field, whose only prime ideal is $0$, so $\dim(A^\wedge/\mathfrak mA^\wedge)=0$ and step 3 gives $\dim A^\wedge=\dim A$. Both are finite: $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, say by $n$ elements, since $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $\dim A\le n$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators].
